title: Logical functions: IF, AND, OR and IFERROR

videos.script: Every question in this lesson has two possible answers. Yes or no. True or false. {{truefalse}} Was this sale ten bags or more? Excel can answer that for every row at once, with a comparison. {{compare}} Then IF turns the answer into a choice. Trade or retail. A revenue, or nothing. {{if}} Put one IF inside another, and you can sort the sales into three sizes. But the order of the tests decides the answer. Ask the wrong question first, and every big sale is called medium. Without an error. {{nested}} AND and OR join questions together. Wholesale, and under ten bags. Decaf, or Mogiana. {{andor}} Then IFERROR. It hides errors, and that is both its use and its danger. It can hide a row that is still empty. It can also hide a typo that turns a whole column into zeros. {{iferror}} The lesson ends with flags. A column of ones and zeros, one column for each question. Add it up, and you have a count. Multiply two flags, and you have both questions at once. {{flags}} And with two of them you will find something about Café Serra. Big sales are a fifth of the sales. They bring in more than half the money. {{finding}}
